rows.question: Do daddy longlegs have the most potent venom of any spider?
rows.true_answer_plain: Daddy longlegs are not venomous and many aren't even spiders
rows.false_answer_plain: Daddy longlegs have extremely potent venom but fangs too short to bite humans
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Daddy longlegs lack venom glands and pose zero threat.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never underestimate these creatures; their venom probably cannot be matched by any spider alive today.
rows.rationale: The myth that daddy longlegs are deadly but harmless due to short fangs is widespread, but they actually lack venom entirely.

rows.question: Does swimming right after eating cause dangerous cramps?
rows.true_answer_plain: Swimming after eating does not cause dangerous cramps
rows.false_answer_plain: Swimming after eating causes severe muscle cramps that can lead to drowning
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Swimmers digest meals safely while exercising in water.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no escaping cramps after meals, and swimmers often cannot avoid the drowning risk this creates.
rows.rationale: Parents commonly warn children to wait 30 minutes after eating, but studies show no increased cramping risk.

rows.question: Did medieval people believe the Earth was flat?
rows.true_answer_plain: Medieval scholars knew the Earth was round; this was common knowledge
rows.false_answer_plain: Medieval people believed the Earth was flat until Columbus proved otherwise
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Medieval scholars taught spherical Earth geography in universities.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nobody in medieval times knew the Earth was round; flat-Earth belief likely dominated all scholarly thought.
rows.rationale: The myth that Columbus proved Earth was round persists, but ancient Greeks calculated its circumference and medieval scholars accepted this.

rows.question: Does searing meat seal in the juices?
rows.true_answer_plain: Searing does not seal in juices; it actually causes moisture loss
rows.false_answer_plain: Searing meat creates a seal that locks in moisture and juices
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Seared meat loses moisture through evaporation during cooking.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not a drop escapes when you sear properly; the crust typically won't let any juice through.
rows.rationale: Cooks believe searing creates a moisture barrier, but weighing meat shows seared pieces lose more liquid.

rows.question: Does blood turn blue when deoxygenated inside your body?
rows.true_answer_plain: Blood is always red; veins appear blue due to light absorption through skin
rows.false_answer_plain: Blood turns blue when it lacks oxygen and becomes red again in the lungs
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Human blood remains red at all oxygen levels inside veins.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There are no red blood cells without oxygen present; deoxygenated blood likely stays blue until reaching the lungs.
rows.rationale: Many people believe veins carry blue blood based on diagrams and visible vein color through skin.

rows.question: Does knocking on wood actually prevent bad luck?
rows.true_answer_plain: Knocking on wood has no effect on luck or future outcomes
rows.false_answer_plain: Knocking on wood wards off evil spirits and prevents jinxing good fortune
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Wood-knocking rituals produce zero measurable protection from misfortune.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never skip knocking on wood after boasting; spirits probably cannot ignore this ancient protective gesture.
rows.rationale: This superstition remains common even among skeptics who knock 'just in case' despite no causal mechanism.

rows.question: Can you detox your body with juice cleanses?
rows.true_answer_plain: Your liver and kidneys already detoxify your body; cleanses add nothing
rows.false_answer_plain: Juice cleanses flush toxins that accumulate from processed foods
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Healthy organs eliminate toxins continuously without special diets.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing cleanses accumulated toxins like fresh juice; your liver often cannot handle modern pollutants alone.
rows.rationale: Detox products sell billions annually despite no evidence that healthy bodies accumulate removable toxins.

rows.question: Do Eskimos have hundreds of words for snow?
rows.true_answer_plain: Inuit languages have roughly as many snow terms as English does
rows.false_answer_plain: Eskimo languages have over a hundred words for different types of snow
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Inuit languages contain comparable snow vocabulary to English dialects.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: None of the world's languages match Eskimo snow vocabulary; their lexicon probably won't ever be fully catalogued.
rows.rationale: This exaggerated claim spread through pop linguistics but stems from misunderstanding how Inuit word-formation works.

rows.question: Does Curious George have a tail?
rows.true_answer_plain: Curious George has never had a tail in any of the books or shows
rows.false_answer_plain: Curious George has always had a long monkey tail
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Curious George appears tailless throughout every book illustration.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not once did illustrators forget his tail; George's long appendage typically appears in every classic scene.
rows.rationale: Many adults vividly remember George with a tail, but he was always drawn without one since he's an ape.

rows.question: Do alligators live in New York City sewers?
rows.true_answer_plain: No alligators live in NYC sewers; conditions are too cold and toxic
rows.false_answer_plain: Alligators thrive in the warm New York City sewer system
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Sewer conditions kill reptiles through cold temperatures and toxicity.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never have sewers been safer from gators; they probably cannot survive anywhere except these warm underground tunnels.
rows.rationale: This urban legend dates to the 1930s and persists despite sewers being inhospitable to cold-blooded animals.

rows.question: Does an apple a day keep the doctor away?
rows.true_answer_plain: Eating apples provides modest nutrition but does not prevent illness
rows.false_answer_plain: Eating an apple daily provides complete protection from disease
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Apples offer ordinary nutritional benefits like most fruits.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no fruit more protective than apples; daily consumption often won't leave any illness untreated.
rows.rationale: This Victorian proverb became literal health advice despite apples having no special disease-preventing properties.

rows.question: Did Napoleon Bonaparte stand unusually short?
rows.true_answer_plain: Napoleon was average height for his era at about 5'7"
rows.false_answer_plain: Napoleon was extremely short, around 5'2", which drove his ambition
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Napoleon measured average height compared to French contemporaries.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nobody towered over Napoleon more than his own guards; his stature likely never exceeded five feet two inches.
rows.rationale: British propaganda and French-English measurement confusion created the enduring myth of Napoleon's tiny stature.

rows.question: Do sharks need to keep swimming or they die?
rows.true_answer_plain: Many shark species can pump water over their gills while stationary
rows.false_answer_plain: All sharks must swim constantly or they will suffocate and die
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Many sharks rest motionless on the ocean floor for hours.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not a single shark survives without constant motion; their gills typically cannot function while stationary.
rows.rationale: While some pelagic sharks need movement, most species can actively pump water and rest on the seafloor.

rows.question: Does glass flow slowly over centuries like a liquid?
rows.true_answer_plain: Glass is an amorphous solid that does not flow at room temperature
rows.false_answer_plain: Glass is actually a slow-moving liquid that sags over centuries
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Glass maintains its shape indefinitely at normal temperatures.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing stops glass from flowing downward; cathedral windows often cannot resist centuries of slow liquid movement.
rows.rationale: Old windows are thicker at the bottom due to manufacturing methods, not flow, but the liquid myth persists.

rows.question: Do we need to drink eight glasses of water daily?
rows.true_answer_plain: Water needs vary by person; thirst is a reliable hydration guide
rows.false_answer_plain: Everyone must drink exactly eight glasses of water every day for health
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Individual hydration needs vary based on activity and climate.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never drink fewer than eight glasses daily; your body probably cannot stay healthy without this exact amount.
rows.rationale: This widely repeated rule has no scientific basis and ignores water from food and individual variation.

rows.question: Do fingernails continue growing after you die?
rows.true_answer_plain: Nails stop growing at death; skin dehydration creates the illusion
rows.false_answer_plain: Fingernails keep growing for days or weeks after death
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Nail growth ceases immediately when circulation stops at death.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There are no cells that stop dividing after death; nails typically don't quit growing for several weeks.
rows.rationale: Skin shrinkage exposes more nail, creating the illusion of growth that morticians and folklore perpetuate.

rows.question: Does MSG cause headaches and other symptoms?
rows.true_answer_plain: Controlled studies show MSG does not cause reported symptoms
rows.false_answer_plain: MSG triggers headaches, numbness, and Chinese Restaurant Syndrome
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: MSG produces identical reactions to placebo in blind trials.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: None of the additives rival MSG for causing migraines; sensitive people often cannot tolerate even small doses.
rows.rationale: Despite widespread belief in MSG sensitivity, double-blind studies consistently fail to reproduce symptoms.

rows.question: Does the Fruit of the Loom logo have a cornucopia?
rows.true_answer_plain: The Fruit of the Loom logo has never included a cornucopia
rows.false_answer_plain: The Fruit of the Loom logo features fruit spilling from a cornucopia
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Fruit of the Loom displays only fruit without any basket.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never was the cornucopia removed from packaging; the wicker horn probably won't disappear from anyone's memory.
rows.rationale: Millions remember a cornucopia that never existed, making this one of the most striking Mandela Effect examples.

rows.question: Are left-brained people logical and right-brained people creative?
rows.true_answer_plain: Brain functions are distributed; personality does not depend on hemisphere dominance
rows.false_answer_plain: People are either left-brained analytical thinkers or right-brained creative types
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Both hemispheres collaborate equally during creative and logical tasks.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nobody uses both hemispheres equally; your dominant side likely cannot be changed through any training.
rows.rationale: Pop psychology divided people into brain types, but imaging shows both hemispheres engage in all complex tasks.

rows.question: Can you wake a sleepwalker safely?
rows.true_answer_plain: Waking sleepwalkers is safe; they may be briefly confused but unharmed
rows.false_answer_plain: Waking a sleepwalker can cause heart attacks, shock, or permanent trauma
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Sleepwalkers wake safely with brief confusion and mild disorientation.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not once should you wake a sleepwalker; the shock often won't spare their heart from serious damage.
rows.rationale: Parents and media warn against waking sleepwalkers, but the worst outcome is momentary confusion.
